...A woman is holding me.
Mother.

Facing Mother, one man is there.
—Father.

To Father, Mother speaks. Each word goes in like a point.

"You are not her father."

Mother says it.

"You must not think yourself this child's father."

"This child is my daughter. Mine alone."

"This child has no father."

"This child is not your daughter."

Father listens. No answer.

From his face, I know. Choosing is not in his hands.
Only the decision is being given to him.

Mother says it again.

"This child has no father."

—No father for me.

"You are not this child's father."

—This man is not my father.

"This child...◆you must not love her."

Then I—
From this man, I will have no love.

en.html:
Greed had not been my intention. The bag of fresh fruit was making a strong case against me, all the same. Its cord bit into my fingertips; now this hand, now that, I carried it home.

A gift, they had said. Very kind. Free fruit. Only the fingers were being charged. Left hand suffered, so I transferred the happiness to the right. Right hand immediately understood the left hand's position. Neither wished to be ungrateful, but both were developing strong opinions about generosity. Arre, what was I to do? Put the fruit back? Then it would rot, and apparently preventing that tragedy was also my responsibility. I had left work carrying more work, except this work could be eaten.

Dusk meant people everywhere. Children and students going home, mothers and daughters buying things for dinner. Even this sleepy northern Kanto town had its lively hour. This one only.

One in four faces I passed, I knew. A small bow from me, a small bow in return. We went on.

Sometimes I stopped for a little conversation. Usually the neighborhood ladies, who had plenty of conversation available.

The subject seemed less important than the opportunity to move the mouth. I nodded and supplied the appropriate haan, haan. No hardship on my side. The subjects themselves, though, were mostly unhappy ones.

Yamato, Koryu 39.
What the history books would make of this time and place, how was I to know? For those of us living in it, the urge was to give up on the present and put our hopes somewhere ahead.

Four years only since the war's tragic end. The Rokuhara shogunate, which had staged that tragedy's final act, was busy securing its rule through violent repression across the country.

The Osaka Massacre. That great event of earlier years, never spoken of in public, was still burned fresh into people's hearts.
...If we resist, our town will become like that also, no? Bhagwan bachaye.

With those words, Mrs. Yabe from Third District went toward the greengrocer. I too resumed my walk home.

Probably everywhere in Yamato, people were saying much the same thing. But from the mouths of people here, perhaps the tension was a little different.

...Considering our town's present situation, that was understandable.

　夕暮れ時だけに、人出は多かった。

母親や娘。北関東の<ruby>鄙<rt>ひな</rt></ruby>びた田舎町も、この時刻ばかり
は賑々しい。

　行き会う人間の四人に一人は顔見知りだ。
　会釈をし合ってすれ違う。

　時折、足を止めて短い世間話をすることもある。
　相手は大概、話好きなご近所の奥様方だ。

　話の内容がというより口を動かすこと自体が楽しい
様子の相手に、頷きながら相槌を返す。こちらとして
も別段、苦痛を覚えるような作業ではない。
　とはいえ話題の多くは楽しからぬものだった。

　興隆三九年、大和――
　この時空間が歴史書にどう記されるかなど知る由も
ないが、実際に生きる人間としては、早々に現在に見
切りをつけて未来を想いたくなる時代ではある。

　悲劇的な終戦からまだ四年。
　その悲劇の最後の一幕を演出した六波羅幕府は支配
の礎を固めるため、各地での弾圧暴挙に余念がない。

　公の場では決して語られない先年の大事件――大阪
虐殺は、それでも人々の心に生々しく焼き付いている。
　……逆らえばこの町もああなっちゃうんだろうねえ。
くわばら、くわばら。

　そう言って、三丁目の矢部さんは八百屋の方へ歩い
ていった。
　俺も家に向かって歩き出す。

　矢部さんの去り際の言葉は、大和全国、何処の誰も
が呟いているようなことだろう。
　だがこの町の人間が口にするそれは、ほかに比べて
緊張感が少しばかり違ったかもしれない。

　……町の<ruby>現況<rt>・・</rt></ruby>を思えば、無理からぬことだが。

en.html:
Now that I looked around, the town itself had changed a little.

The shogunate did not allow people to move wherever they pleased. Even so, unable to bear the hardship, quite a few had slipped away in the night.
...Until recently, a house on this street had kept dogs.

Every time I passed, so many barking together. What a racket.
Now, nothing. All those faithful dogs had been killed. Their dog-loving owner had disappeared, who knew when.

...Until recently, children had play equipment in that park.
That also was gone. Taken away for barricade materials, apparently.

No dogs barking. No children cheering.
Two things only, taken away. And the whole street felt different.

...No.
That was not right.

The town center gave way to farmland. Beyond that, among the trees, the large estate came into view.
My house—no, that was taking rather a lot upon myself. The Minato house, where I lived.

For the size, two reasons were available. Here in the countryside, land was not in short supply. And this was a branch of the family that had ruled the district since ancient times: in practice always, and sometimes officially also.

A reason for the size, yes. A use for it? Doubtful.
The larger is supposed to do everything the smaller can. For a family of three, this one mainly supplied extra space in which to be inconvenienced.

Aadmi teen, makaan poora raajya. Three people, one entire kingdom of a house. Go to speak to somebody, and first the legs must prove their loyalty to the family. All that empty space, and somehow the occupants are the ones who must adjust.

An apartment would make life so much easier.
But the Minato family, in an apartment? Such conduct would never be permitted. The ancestors require room. Unlike the living, they do not have to walk across it.

The old man answered the voice from the doorway with a snort and walked away. His steps acknowledged his age, whether he did or not; they were a little unsteady. Still, I could not offer to escort him. That sort of consideration, from me, would receive no thanks. I knew him well enough.

It seemed he meant to go on playing the mighty king, with advancing age refused admission. The knees, unfortunately, had heard nothing about this arrangement. A man can frighten the whole household into agreement; try the same glare on your own knees. They are inside the kingdom only, yet openly conducting opposition. Offer him an arm, however, and suddenly you are the rebel. Achha. Let the king negotiate directly with the road.

No car either. I watched him set off down the dark road, then turned to the person who had been watching beside me.
